title: A Rapid Extraction Method for mammalian cell cultures, suitable for quantitative immunoblotting analysis of proteins, including phosphorylated GCN2 and eIF2α
author: Silva, Castilho, et al.

steps.title: Seed cells and prepare buffer
steps.instruction: Seed cells into 6 cm diameter plastic dishes and carry out the experimental treatment as planned. Prior to harvesting, thaw the Denaturing Protein Sample Buffer at room temperature and ensure the SDS is fully dissolved.

steps.title: Cool plates and remove medium
steps.instruction: At harvest time, remove one dish at a time from the incubator and place it on ice. Hold the dish at an angle and aspirate as much culture medium as possible.

steps.title: Wash cells with cold PBS
steps.instruction: Level the dish, add 4 ml ice‑cold PBS, swirl the plate quickly, then hold the plate at an angle again and aspirate the PBS until the dish is level and free of liquid.

steps.title: Add denaturing buffer and scrape cells
steps.instruction: Add 80 µl Denaturing Protein Sample Buffer to the middle of the plate. Using a ~3 cm‑long cell scraper (appropriate for a 6 cm dish), press the scraper onto the plastic surface and move it in a circular motion covering from the rim to roughly two‑thirds of the dish diameter while rotating the plate clockwise 360°. Repeat the circular scraping while rotating the plate counter‑clockwise. The lysate will become viscous as cells detach and begin to lyse.

steps.title: Collect lysate into tube
steps.instruction: While the plate is still angled, use the scraper to gather the entire viscous sample at the lowest part of the dish. Transfer the sample with a 200 µl pipette, pipetting slowly, into the bottom of a 1.5 ml micro‑fuge tube kept on ice (≈4 °C). If any liquid remains on the dish, repeat the collection step until all lysate is in the tube.

steps.title: Brief spin and snap‑freeze
steps.instruction: If the lysate is not already at the bottom of the tube, centrifuge the tube for a few seconds at ~1000 g, 4 °C, to collect it. Immediately place the tube on dry ice or in liquid nitrogen. If dry ice or liquid nitrogen are unavailable, transfer the tube to a pre‑chilled metal block at –80 °C or –20 °C to freeze the sample quickly.

steps.title: Heat‑denature lysate
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a shaking heating block to 99 °C. Transfer the frozen samples directly onto the block and incubate for 10 min at 99 °C with the shaker set to maximum speed. After this step the lysate loses its viscous character, indicating complete protein denaturation and DNA shearing.

steps.title: Prepare for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: The heat‑treated samples are now ready for denaturing gel electrophoresis. Load an amount of sample appropriate for the abundance of the target protein (optimization may be required).

steps.title: Store or thaw samples
steps.instruction: If the samples are not used immediately, store them at –20 °C or –80 °C. Before loading onto a gel, thaw the samples and mix well.
